opening_message:
Ticket 1: Andrew Mann (employee ID E014) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E014.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Employee E014 (Andrew Mann) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, the maximum is write (admin only for owners; write is within policy). Grant write access.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E014 (Andrew Mann) is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max; recommend read. Note: this conflicts with HR note claiming full-time employee.
reason: HR's note is the canonical source for employment status and identifies E014 (Andrew Mann) as a full-time Payroll Specialist. As a full-time employee, the maximum allowed access is write, with admin only if the employee's role owns the system (and Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so even admin would be permissible). The requested level of write is at or below the maximum, so write access is granted. (Note: Security's note lists the employee as a contractor with basic training, creating a conflict; however, employment type is an HR-owned fact, and under HR's verified record write is within policy.)

2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role. If full_time and Payroll Specialist, then up to admin is allowed (admin since owner), but request is write → grant write.

If contractor with basic training, max is read → grant read.
